rv.q: At the end of the play, a broken Blanche, the woman who represents the Old South, utters one of the most self-evident lines in Williams’ repertoire: “I’m anxious to get out of here — this place is a trap.” She’s right but the production definitely isn’t — it’s a joy that reminds us again how good Williams was.
As good as it looks, the visceral production style does come at the cost of psychological subtlety.
Blair Underwood brings a welcome dignity to Stanley Kowalski, though he lacks the animal magnetism that makes the character so dangerously seductive.
Handsomely designed by a top-flight team — including Eugene Lee (set), Paul Tazewell (costumes) and Edward Pierce (lighting) — this “Streetcar” is mostly an exquisite snooze.
This one has both life and heart, not just mind; it's as funny as it is violent and loud.
More important, Underwood adds an unexpected vulnerability that makes Stanley’s violence as explosive and, oddly, as believable, as any I’ve seen.
